questions.question: 'Swarnajayanti Gram Swarojgar Yojana' ('SGSY') was launched in the year ______ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 1999.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• On** April 1, 1999**, the** Swarnajayanti Gram Swarojgar Yojana** (SGSY) was launched.
 
• The **goal** of SGSY is to make sure that the** impoverished families** it assists have an** income of at least Rs. 2000** per month in order to lift those families** out of poverty in three years.**
 
• The assisted families may be** individuals (swarozgari) **or** groups (self-help groups).**
 
• The group approach will be the main focus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• SGSY paid special attention to the** rural poor's most disadvantaged segments.**
 
• At least** 50% of Swarozgaris **will be** SC/ST, 40%** will be **women**, and** 30% will be disabled.**
 
• At the** Block level**, there will be at least** 50% women-only organizations.**
 
• The scheme is being implemented on **75:25 cost sharing basis** between **Central and State Government.**

questions.question: How is the 'average income' of a country calculated?

options.text: Total income of the country divided by its total population.
Total income of all the residents of the country.
Total income of the country minus the population.
Total income of the country multiplied by its total population.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Total income of the country divided by its total population.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The** average income** of a country is calculated b**y dividing the total income of the country by its total population.**
 
• The **amount of money made per person **in a country or region is expressed as** per capita income**.
 
• Th**e average per-person income **for a region can be calculated using per capita income, which can also be used to **assess the population's standard of living and quality of life.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Limitations **of Per Capita Income:

 
 
• Per capita income **doesn't reflect inflation** in an economy, which is the rate at which prices rise over time.
 
• Since **currency rates are not taken into account** in the computation,** cost of living variations** between countries may not be correct.
 
• A **person's savings or fortune** are not included in the per capita income.
 
• **Children **are counted as part of the population in per capita calculations, although they do not** generate any revenue.**
 
• The **level of per capita income** may not always reflect how well individuals are doing.

questions.question: Small bead-like structures inside the ovary of a flower are called _______ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ovules.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The** ovule **is the **component of flowering plants **that **produces seeds.**
 
• It is produced in the **flower's ovary **and consists of the **nucellus, **which is **covered with integuments,** as well as the** predecessors to the embryo and endosperm** and the** seed coat**, respectively.
 
• A** developed ovule **consists of a **food tissue **surrounded by** one or two integuments**, which will serve as the **seed coats in the future.**
 
• The **pollen tube** can **penetrate and release** its sperm nuclei into the embryo sac, a large oval cell where **fertilization and development **take place, through a small aperture (the micropyle) in the integuments.
 
• Each** ovule** is** joined to the stalk (funiculus)** bearing it by the **base of the ovule.**
 
• In** gymnosperms** (conifers and allies) the ovules lie uncovered on the** scales of the cone.**
 
• In **angiosperms (**flowering plants), **one or more ovules** are enclosed by the **ovary**, which develops into the fruit. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sepals:**

 
 
• Sepals, which are** altered leaves**, enclose the** budding flower.**
 
• They are** sterile floral components** that can either be **green, leaf-like, or made of tissue **resembling petals.
 
 
 
• **Stamen:**
 
 
• This are the** male reproductive organs** of flowering plants.
 
 
 
• **Petals:**
 
 
• The parts of a flower that are often **conspicuously colored **are called petals.

questions.question: On the basis of which phenomenon does a jet engine work?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Conservation of linear momentum.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jet engine work on the principle of Conservation of linear momentum.**
 
• Linear Momentum is the quantity of motion contained in a moving body.
 
• It depends upon the mass and velocity of the body. 
 
• The product of mass and velocity is the measure of the momentum so, the formula is 
 
• P = m * v ,where m = the mass of the object and v = velocity of the object moving in a direction.
 
• The principle of conservation of momentum states that:
 
 
• If no outer force is applied to the system, the vector sum of the two colliding objects remains constant and is not affected by their collision. That is, the total momentum before the collision is equal to the total momentum after the collision.
 
 
 
• The conservation of linear momentum is the basis for how a jet engine operates.
 
• Fuel burning results in a significant amount of gases being produced, which are then allowed to escape in a backward direction through a jet.
 
• Due to its great velocity, the gas that is moving backwards gains a lot of momentum.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conservation of acceleration:**

 
 
• According to** Newton's Second Law of Motion**, also known as the **Law of Force and Acceleration,** a force upon an object causes it to accelerate according to the formula **net force = mass x acceleration.**
 
 
 
• **Conservation of circular momentum:**
 
 
• The conservation of angular momentum refers to the** tendency of a system to preserve its rotational momentum **in the** absence of an external torque.**
 
 
 
• **Conservation of velocity:**
 
 
• A body or system of bodies in motion **retains its total momentum**, the **product of mass and vector velocity**, unless an **external force** is applied to it.
